'''Brian Smith''' is an American [[portrait photography|portrait photographer]] and [[photojournalist]]. He may be known best for portraits of actors, business leaders, politicians, and athletes that are at once stylish and telling.<ref>Schonauer, David, [http://www.ai-ap.com/publications/article/4221/preview-photographer-brian-smiths-portrait-secr.html "Preview: Photographer Brian Smith's Portrait Secrets"], ''Pro Photo Daily'', October 5, 2012.</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Born in [[Ames, Iowa]], Smith got his start in photography in high school as a stringer for the ''[[Ames Tribune]]''. He received his bachelor's degree in [[journalism]] from the [[University of Missouri]]. As a 20-year-old student there,<ref>[http://journalism.missouri.edu/alum/brian-smith/ University of Missouri Journalism Alumni]</ref> his first magazine photograph was published in [[Life (magazine)|''Life'']] magazine, showing the [[New York Yankees]] manager [[Billy Martin]] crying at the funeral of his player [[Thurman Munson]].

== Career ==
Smith's portraits of celebrities, athletes and business executives have appeared on the covers of magazines, including his photograph of [[Pope John Paul II]], which was featured on the cover of the ''[[Newsweek]]'' Commemorative issue.<ref>''Newsweek'', April 11, 2005.</ref>

The book ''Art & Soul'' features Smith's portraits of celebrities accompanied by personal testimonials from each artist expressing their support for the importance of the arts in their lives.<ref>[http://thecreativecoalition.org/2011/10/28/art-soul-book-launches-in-los-angeles/ ''Art & Soul'' book launch].</ref>

Smith is President of Editorial Photographers (EP),<ref>[http://www.editorialphoto.com/resources/asmp_qa.asp Editorial Photographers].</ref> a photography trade organization of magazine photographers and photojournalists from around the world. He has lectured students on the Business of Editorial Photography at [[Brooks Institute of Photography]], [[Ohio University]], [[Hallmark Institute]]<ref>[http://hallmark.edu/events/ Brian Smith Speaks at Hallmark Institute of Photography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100527123313/http://hallmark.edu/events/ |date=2010-05-27 }}.</ref> and the Atlanta and Fort Lauderdale [[Art Institutes]].

His television appearances include guest appearances on ''[[The X Factor (U.S.)|The X Factor]]''<ref>"One of Ten Voted Off", ''The X Factor'', November 17, 2011.</ref> and [[Fine Living Network]]<ref>"Me -vs- Me: Sports Photography", Fine Living Network, October 8, 2006.</ref> Smith has been featured in the ''Photo District News'' Portraiture Issue, the ''[[Communication Arts]]'' Photography Annual, and ''Pop Photo''.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

== Personal life ==
He lives in [[Miami Beach]], Florida, with his wife Fazia Ali, a [[fashion stylist]]. He is the son of [[Gerald W. Smith]], author of the textbook ''Engineering Economy: Analysis of Capital Expenditures'', emeritus Professor at [[Iowa State University]] in Ames.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

==Awards and honors==
Smith was a member{{citation needed|date=October 2013}} of the ''[[Orange County Register]]'' photography staff that won the 1985 [[Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography]] recognizing its coverage of the [[1984 Summer Olympics|1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games]].<ref name=Pulitzer>[http://www.pulitzer.org/bycat/Spot-News-Photography "Spot News Photography"]. The Pulitzer Prizes. Retrieved 2009-05-18.</ref> In 1988 he and [[Carol Guzy]] were finalists for their photographs of [[Haiti]] in turmoil, published by the ''[[Miami Herald]]''.<ref name=Pulitzer/>

His photograph of [[Greg Louganis]] hitting his head on the [[Diving (sport)|diving]] board at the [[1988 Summer Olympics|1988 Seoul Olympic Games]] won first prize in the Sports category of the 1988 [[World Press Photo]],<ref name="World Press Photo">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130416050048/http://www.archive.worldpressphoto.org/search/layout/result/indeling/detailwpp/form/wpp/q/ishoofdafbeelding/true/trefwoord/year/1988/trefwoord/category/Sports|title=World Press Photo 1988}}. Retrieved 2009-12-14.</ref> and was included in ''[[Photo District News]]'' as a memorable sports photograph.<ref>[http://www.pdngallery.com/20years/sports/20_brian_smith.html ''Photo District News'' 20th Anniversary Issue].</ref>
